content: 1. Doxycycline reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction is relevant only for oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and close monitoring are advised. 2. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Drospirenone slightly increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain, but monitoring is advised. 4. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 5. Eluxadoline increases the levels of conjugated estrogens by reducing their metabolism. It may also increase systemic exposure to co-administered OATP1B1 substrates. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 6. Encorafenib affects the metabolism of conjugated estrogens by both inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may lead to increased toxicity or reduced efficacy. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 7. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of enoxaparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated, and alternative therapies should be used. 8. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Ertapenem decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and close monitoring are advised. 10. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and decreases their levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and close monitoring are necessary. 11. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and erythromycin lactobionate exhibit similar interactions with conjugated estrogens as erythromycin base, affecting both P-glycoprotein and intestinal flora. These interactions apply only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and close monitoring are required. 12. Erythromycin stearate also increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein and decreases their levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and close monitoring are advised. 13. Erythromycin stearate, ethylsuccinate, and lactobionate may also increase the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Elicarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 15. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 16. Conjugated estrogens decrease the levels of exemestane by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain, but monitoring is advised. 17. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of exenatide injectable solution and suspension through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 18. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary, and monitor closely. 19. Felodipine increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 20. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Conjugated estrogens increase the levels or effects of fezolinetant by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to increased AUC and peak plasma concentrations of fezolinetant. 22. Fleroxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and close monitoring are advised. 23. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 24. Fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 25. Conjugated estrogens decrease the levels of folic acid by altering its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain, but monitoring is advised. 26. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of fondaparinux through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. 27. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 28. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 29. Fosfomycin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and close monitoring are advised. 30. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 31. Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and close monitoring are advised. 32. Gentamicin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and close monitoring are recommended. 33. Givosiran increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP1A2 substrates. If unavoidable, reduce the dosage of CYP1A2 substrates and monitor closely. 34. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 35. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 36. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of hemin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may decrease the efficacy of hemin. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 37. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of heparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. 38. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of hyaluronidase by enhancing tissue resistance to the enzyme. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 39. Hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 40. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by strongly inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 41. Conjugated estrogens may interact with imipramine through an unspecified mechanism, potentially altering tricyclic antidepressant effects. The clinical significance is uncertain, but monitoring is advised. 42. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 43. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of insulin degludec and insulin aspart through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 44. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of inhaled insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 45. Conjugated estrogens decrease the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 46. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is uncertain, but monitoring is advised. 47. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary, especially at higher doses of istradefylline. 48. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 49. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 50. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 51. Conjugated estrogens decrease the levels of L-methylfolate by altering its metabolism. The clinical significance is uncertain, but monitoring is advised. 52. Conjugated estrogens decrease the levels of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 53. Lapatinib increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 54. Larotrectinib increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is uncertain, but monitoring is advised. 55. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This effect may persist for up to 9 months after the last dose of lenacapavir. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 56. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and close monitoring are advised. 57. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 58. Linezolid decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and close monitoring are advised. 59. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of liraglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 60. Conjugated estrogens may interact with lofepramine through an unspecified mechanism, potentially altering tricyclic antidepressant effects. The clinical significance is uncertain, but monitoring is advised. 61. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of lonapegsomatropin by reducing serum insulin-like growth factor-1 response. Caution and close monitoring are recommended.
